title: spec_body_amended event payload
$comment: Class: REQUIRES_SPEC_ID. Records a governed amendment to a spec's blast_radius.modules or invariants via `caws specs amend`. Distinct from spec_scope_amended, which covers scope.in/out/support only. Exists because both fields are schema-required non-empty, so `caws specs create` had to emit a scaffolded default, and until this command there was no surface that could replace it on an already-created spec — the discharge route was a hand edit that bypassed the audit trail entirely. On a CLOSED spec the writer permits filling a scaffolded entry but refuses removing or rewriting a substantive one, so this event can never record a retroactive rewrite of what a concluded spec claimed.

added_modules.description: blast_radius.modules entries added by this amendment (may be empty).

removed_modules.description: blast_radius.modules entries removed by this amendment (may be empty).

added_invariants.description: invariants entries added by this amendment (may be empty).

removed_invariants.description: invariants entries removed by this amendment (may be empty).

discharged_scaffold_fields.description: Fields whose scaffolded default was replaced by operator content in this amendment. This is the discriminator that makes an amendment on a closed spec legitimate: a closed spec may have a blank filled and never a claim rewritten.

previous_lifecycle_state.description: The lifecycle state of the amended spec. Recorded because the permitted operations differ by state, so a reader cannot judge the amendment without it.

resulting_modules.description: blast_radius.modules after the amendment. Schema-required non-empty, so the post-state is always assertable.
